source_caption:
Released in 2006, Children of Men is one of those rare films that only seems to get better with time. Directed by Alfonso Cuarón, it imagines a world where no child has been born for 18 years, but beneath its dystopian setting is a deeply human story about hope, compassion, and the importance of never giving up, even when everything feels lost.

What truly sets the film apart is the way it's made. Emmanuel Lubezki's stunning cinematography, especially the unforgettable long takes, pulls you straight into the action and makes every moment feel incredibly real. Nearly two decades later, Children of Men still stands as one of the greatest achievements in modern cinema.
-

source_details.synopsis: Children of Men is a 2006 dystopian action thriller film directed and co-written by Alfonso Cuarón. The screenplay, based on P. D. James' 1992 novel The Children of Men, was credited to five writers, with Clive Owen making additional, uncredited contributions. The film is set in 2027, when two decades of human infertility have left human civilisation on the brink of collapse. Asylum seekers seek sanctuary in the United Kingdom, where they are subjected to detention, deportation and execution by the government.
